term: weak causal connectivity, upstream confluence and source uniqueness
definition: Graph.edge y x points from upstream y to dependent x; Graph.Source x has no incoming graph edge. WeaklyConnected G means every two nodes are related by Mathlib Relation.EqvGen G.edge: a finite undirected zigzag allowing length zero. UniquePredecessor G is Mathlib Relator.LeftUnique G.edge, allowing at most one immediate upstream node at each target. UpstreamConfluent G is standard rewriting confluence of the REVERSED edge: whenever finite reflexive-transitive upstream paths from a reach b and c, those endpoints have finite upstream extensions to some common node (Mathlib Relation.Join). No source, termination, common named root, or uniqueness is in that definition. AtMostOneSource quantifies equality of every pair of Graph.Source nodes, and is vacuous if there are none. WellFoundedEdges is WellFounded G.edge in predecessor orientation. Populated is Nonempty Node. RootedAtUniqueSource says there is one source s, every other source equals s, and every node has a FiniteCausalPath upstream to that same s.
note: Analyst structural profile, with no source attribution. Instantiate G := WorldSourceRegress.actualGraph m w to quantify only existing nodes in a fixed world; connectivity here is causal, not accessibility between worlds. Unique immediate predecessors is a strong open causal restriction. The proved confluence route permits multiple immediate causes, but confluence and connectedness remain open when applied to reality. Neither actual graph WF, necessity, no parts, essence/esse identity, intrinsic explanation, personhood, divine identity nor modal collapse follows. Finite confluence paths need not terminate; WF and population are separate existence inputs.
